ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a square frame with a side length of 10 cm (ignoring the thickness of the frame) is pulled into a quadrilateral $ABCD$. If $\angle BAD=60^\circ$, what is the length of $AC$ in cm?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, construct $DE\perp AB$ intersecting $AB$ at point E, and $CF\perp AB$ at its extension at point F, and connect $AC$,\\
since $AB=BC=CD=AD=10$cm, and $\angle BAD=60^\circ$,\\
thus $DE=CF=AD\times \sin 60^\circ=10\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=5\sqrt{3}$,\\
$BF=BC\times \cos 60^\circ=10\times \frac{1}{2}=5$,\\
in right triangle $AFC$, $AC=\sqrt{AF^{2}+CF^{2}}$,\\
thus $AC=\sqrt{15^{2}+{(5\sqrt{3})}^{2}}=\boxed{10\sqrt{3}}$.
